original_value: Due to its payload, size and computational limits, localizing a micro air vehicle (MAV) using only its onboard sensors in an indoor environment is a challenging problem in practice. This paper introduces an indoor localization approach that relies on only the inertial measurement unit (IMU) and four ultrasonic sensors. Specifically, a novel multi-ray ultrasonic sensor model is proposed to provide a rapid and accurate approximation of the complex beam pattern of the ultrasonic sensors. A fast algorithm for calculating the Jacobian matrix of the measurement function is presented, and then an extended Kalman filter (EKF) is used to fuse the information from the ultrasonic sensors and the IMU. A test based on a MaxSonar MB1222 sensor demonstrates the accuracy of the model, and a simulation and experiment based on the     T h a l e s  I I     MAV platform are conducted. The results indicate good localization performance and robustness against measurement noises.

result.paraphrase: Because of payload, size, and computing constraints, indoor localization of a micro air vehicle (MAV) using only onboard sensors is a difficult practical problem. This paper presents an indoor localization method that uses only an inertial measurement unit (IMU) and four ultrasonic sensors. In particular, it proposes a new multi-ray ultrasonic sensor model to quickly and accurately approximate the sensors’ complex beam pattern. It also provides a fast method for computing the Jacobian matrix of the measurement function, after which an extended Kalman filter (EKF) fuses data from the ultrasonic sensors and the IMU. A test with a MaxSonar MB1222 sensor validates the model’s accuracy, and simulations and experiments are performed on the T h a l e s  I I MAV platform. The results show strong localization performance and robustness to measurement noise.
